issues.description: Interrupted first session/lease publication previously left original-book discovery and attachment blocked.
Discovery and initial metadata/handle publication are serialized by one book-root cross-process lock; initialization also takes the session lock.
If initial lease publication succeeds but its fsync/verification reports failure before a handle escapes, only the current initialization lease is detached.

verification.skip_reason: requires a real Windows process handle
verification.command: PYTHONPATH=tests PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_platform_chrome_initialization tests.test_platform_chrome_bridge tests.test_workbench_archives.WorkbenchArchivesTests.test_restored_bridge_reconnects_and_unknown_save_requires_reconciliation tests.test_workbench_archives.WorkbenchArchivesTests.test_restored_live_bridge_is_inert_and_old_handle_cannot_resume_requests tests.test_workbench_archives.WorkbenchArchivesTests.test_restore_reconnects_after_real_process_exit_before_first_session_publication tests.test_workbench_archives.WorkbenchArchivesTests.test_restored_old_handles_never_touch_missing_or_empty_locks_and_missing_sessions -v

boundaries: Only incomplete, never-ready metadata with no published lease or request/health/unknown payload may be ignored; files are preserved.
Existing live leases and unknown request evidence are never erased or reused.
Restored evidence remains inert and old handles remain rejected.
No real platform, installed plugin, release or native Windows validation performed.

A hard process exit after lease publication but before handle publication cannot run cleanup: the valid lease remains until normal expiry and is never treated as empty initialization residue. Immediate recovery of that case is not claimed.
